requirements.name: PSR Mandatory Reimbursement — 5 Business Day SLA
requirements.description: The customer must receive their reimbursement credit within 5 business days of submitting the fraud claim (FraudCase trigger). This is a mandatory statutory obligation under PSR PS23/3 (GOV-003-R01). The clock starts at FraudCaseCreated (customer_report trigger) and stops at ReimbursementCredited. The full investigation, decision, and credit execution must complete within this window.
requirements.target: 100% of approved and partial reimbursement claims credited within 5 business days of FraudCase creation
requirements.measurement: ReimbursementCredited.credited_at minus FraudCase.reported_date, in business days (UK business day calendar). Measured per case and reported monthly to PSR (GOV-003-R01).
requirements.breach_consequence: PSR enforcement action under Payment Systems Act 2013. Financial penalty up to 10% of annual turnover. Mandatory remediation plan.
requirements.stop_the_clock_exception: The 5-business-day SLA may be stopped only where suspected fraud-by-customer is under active investigation (EX-005). Senior Manager (PER-059) must authorise the stop-the-clock. Maximum stop-the-clock extension: 35 business days (PSR guidance).

requirements.name: Case Creation SLA — 4 Hours from Report
requirements.description: A FraudCase must be created and a Fraud Analyst assigned within 4 hours of the customer report being received. This SLA ensures that investigation begins promptly, preserving evidence integrity (device data, session data) and giving the bank sufficient time to complete the investigation within the 5-business-day PSR window.
requirements.target: 99% of FraudCases assigned to an analyst within 4 hours of FraudCaseCreated
requirements.measurement: FraudCase.assigned_analyst timestamp minus FraudCase.created_at. P99 <= 4 hours. Out-of-hours cases: 4 hours measured from start of next UK business day.
requirements.owned_by: SVC-013 (case management queue), Fraud Operations team scheduling

requirements.name: Outcome Letter — Regulated Communication within 5 Business Days
requirements.description: The outcome letter (approve, partial, or decline) must be dispatched to the customer within 5 business days of the fraud report, regardless of whether it accompanies a credit or is a standalone decline. The letter must meet PSR and Consumer Duty content requirements: plain English, FOS signpost on declines, quantified reimbursement amount on approvals.
requirements.target: 100% of outcome letters dispatched within 5 business days
requirements.owned_by: SVC-053 (Notification Service), triggered by FraudReimbursementApproved or FraudReimbursementDeclined event

requirements.name: PSR Quarterly Reporting — Claims Data Accuracy
requirements.description: The bank must submit accurate quarterly APP fraud claims data to the PSR: total claims received, total approved, total declined, total partial, average reimbursement amount, and recovery rates. Data must be derived from FraudCase and ReimbursementClaim entities.
requirements.target: 100% data completeness. Zero material restatements in PSR quarterly returns.
requirements.measurement: Quarterly reconciliation of FraudCase counts against PSR submission

requirements.name: Fraud Case Management — Availability
requirements.description: SVC-013 (Fraud Detection) case management APIs must be available 99.95% of the time, measured monthly. Fraud reporting and investigation must remain accessible to customers and analysts during all business hours. Real-time fraud scoring (sub-flow 1) has its own availability obligation inherited from JRN-002.
requirements.target: 99.95% monthly availability for POST /fraud-cases, GET /fraud-cases/{id}, PATCH /fraud-cases/{id}
requirements.measurement: Synthetic monitoring from two independent UK data centre locations. Latency SLA: P99 < 2,000ms for POST /fraud-cases (case creation), P99 < 500ms for GET /fraud-cases/{id} (read operations).
requirements.breach_consequence: SLA breach triggers PRA operational resilience IBS reporting obligation (GOV-004-R02). APP fraud reporting is classified as an Important Business Service.
requirements.planned_maintenance_window: Maximum 4 hours per calendar month, scheduled outside 07:00–22:00 UK time. Must not exceed 2 consecutive maintenance windows.
requirements.rpo: Recovery Point Objective: 5 minutes (WORM audit records must not be lost beyond this window)
requirements.rto: Recovery Time Objective: 30 minutes for full case management capability restoration

requirements.name: Reimbursement Credit Execution — Availability
requirements.description: SVC-001 (Retail Banking Core) reimbursement credit function must maintain 99.95% availability. A reimbursement credit failure must trigger an immediate retry with exponential backoff. If credit cannot be applied within 2 hours of FraudReimbursementApproved event, the case is escalated to the Fraud Operations duty manager.
requirements.target: 99.95% availability for reimbursement credit operations. Zero failed credits without retry.
requirements.measurement: ReimbursementCredited event timestamp gap from FraudReimbursementApproved. Alert threshold: gap > 2 hours.

requirements.name: Customer Fraud Reporting Channel — Mobile App
requirements.description: The 'Report Fraud' journey within CH-002 (Mobile App) must be available 99.9% of the time. Fraud reporting is a time-sensitive function — a customer who cannot report in the app may call the fraud line (CH-004), but app unavailability must be minimised. App unavailability during a fraud incident increases case complexity.
requirements.target: 99.9% availability for the mobile app fraud reporting flow
requirements.fallback: If mobile app is unavailable: telephony channel (CH-004) must remain available 24/7 at 99.9% availability

requirements.name: WORM Retention — 7-Year Immutable Storage
requirements.description: All FraudCase, FraudEvidence, and ReimbursementClaim records must be retained in WORM (Write Once Read Many) immutable storage for a minimum of 7 years from case closure date. This covers both the regulatory evidence obligation (PSR PS23/3 enforcement, FCA BCOBS audit) and the FOS complaint reference period (6 months from decision, with a maximum 3-year lookback under FOS rules, extended to 7 years for financial records under FCA BCOBS). Records must be producible within 2 business days of a regulatory request.
requirements.target: 100% of FraudCase records archived to SVC-111 (WORM Compliance Store) within 24 hours of FraudCaseClosed event
requirements.measurement: Reconciliation of FraudCase closed count against SVC-111 archive count. Daily automated check.
requirements.worm_storage: SVC-111 (WORM Compliance Store). Append-only. No deletion, modification, or overwrite permitted.
data_included: FraudCase full record including all status transitions
FraudEvidence records and any uploaded customer documents
ReimbursementClaim record including all status updates
All event payloads: FraudCaseCreated through FraudCaseClosed
requirements.governance_reference: GOV-003-R01 (PSR evidence obligation); FCA BCOBS (7-year financial records)

requirements.name: Audit Trail Completeness
requirements.description: Every state transition in the FraudCase lifecycle must be captured as an immutable audit event. The audit trail must allow reconstruction of the complete investigation timeline from FraudCaseCreated to FraudCaseClosed, including every analyst action, evidence item created, decision recorded, and communication dispatched.
requirements.target: Zero gaps in the FraudCase audit trail. Every PATCH operation against FraudCase must generate an audit event in SVC-103.
requirements.measurement: Automated reconciliation between FraudCase.status transition log and SVC-103 audit records. Daily check.

requirements.name: Evidence Document Storage
requirements.description: Customer-provided evidence documents (screenshots, communication logs) uploaded via CH-002 or CH-004 must be encrypted at rest (AES-256), access-controlled to PER-054 and above, and retained for the same 7-year WORM period as the FraudCase record. Documents must not be accessible to PER-001 post-submission (to prevent tampering).
requirements.target: 100% of uploaded documents encrypted at rest. Zero unauthorised access. 7-year retention.

requirements.name: Fraud Case API Latency
requirements.description: SVC-013 Fraud Detection API response time targets for the primary case management operations.

targets.rationale: Case creation involves database write and event publication. Must complete before customer sees confirmation screen.
Read-only case retrieval. P99 under 300ms for analyst UI responsiveness.
Case update with state machine validation.
Decision recording triggers downstream event publication (FraudReimbursementApproved/Declined) and SVC-001 reimbursement workflow initiation.
Evidence submission may include document upload. Async upload to document store; event published synchronously.

requirements.name: Reimbursement Credit Latency
requirements.description: Once FraudReimbursementApproved event is consumed by SVC-001, the credit must be applied to the customer account and the ReimbursementCredited event published within 30 minutes. This ensures the customer sees the credit in their balance promptly after the decision is recorded.
requirements.target: P99 < 30 minutes from FraudReimbursementApproved event to ReimbursementCredited event
requirements.measurement: Event timestamp delta between FraudReimbursementApproved and ReimbursementCredited per case_id

requirements.name: Access Control — Fraud Score and Investigation Data
requirements.description: Fraud scores (PaymentIntent.fraud_score), investigation notes, gross negligence evidence, and the full FraudCase record are restricted to PER-054 (Fraud Analyst), PER-059 (Senior Manager), and PER-052 (MLRO, for SAR referral data). PER-001 (Customer) must never see their own fraud score — disclosure enables fraud evasion. Access control enforced at SVC-013 API layer via JWT role claims.
requirements.enforcement: SVC-013 API validates JWT role claim on every request. Role: fraud_analyst, senior_manager, or mlro required for case detail access. PER-001 JWT has case_status_only scope — returns status, outcome, and reimbursement_amount only.

requirements.name: Evidence Document Access Control
requirements.description: Documents uploaded as FraudEvidence must be accessible only to the assigned fraud analyst and their manager. Documents must not be accessible via the customer-facing mobile app API endpoints. Access log for each document access event must be written to SVC-103.

requirements.name: Outbound Fraud Team Customer Contact — Authentication
requirements.description: All outbound telephone contact from the Fraud Team to PER-001 must be authenticated by the bank to prevent fraudsters impersonating the fraud team. Use of a call-back code or in-app notification for call verification is required. Call authentication protocol must be documented in fraud team operating procedures.
requirements.target: 100% of outbound fraud team calls authenticated via in-app verification before sensitive information is discussed
requirements.owned_by: Fraud Operations team, SVC-017 (in-app call verification notification)

requirements.name: Peak Fraud Campaign Load
requirements.description: The Fraud Detection service must scale to handle a 10x spike in FraudCase creation volume during a major fraud campaign (e.g. a widely publicised impersonation scam targeting the bank's customers). Normal load baseline: 50 new FraudCases per day. Peak load: 500 new FraudCases per day (10x). SVC-013 must auto-scale without degradation of the case creation SLA (4-hour analyst assignment).
requirements.scale_mechanism: SVC-013 deployed as horizontally scalable microservice. Case assignment queue auto-scales with demand. Overflow alerting to Fraud Operations management when queue depth exceeds 2x normal.
